intro.label: development environment
intro.lead: I work on personal projects in my free time, alongside my job. AI helps me speed up parts of development, while a personal VPS lets me publish applications and experiment with infrastructure, deployment, and backend services. I remain in control of the decisions, requirements, and final result.

ai.title: More time to build, less time on repetitive tasks
ai.modeLabel: Select an area where I use AI

intro.label: WHY AI
intro.title: Support during development
intro.description: I use Cursor and Codex to support my development work: they help with technical research, interface implementation, refactoring, and more complex integrations. I use them to work faster, not to delegate product or architecture decisions.

constraint.label: CONSTRAINT // TIME
constraint.title: Time is a real constraint
constraint.description: I work on these projects in my free time, alongside my job. I try to focus that time on the parts that need my input: planning, technical decisions, development, and checking the result.
constraint.outcome: MORE TIME FOR DECISIONS, LESS FOR REPETITIVE TASKS

ui.title: From idea to interface
ui.description: I define the interface’s style, behavior, and goals. AI helps turn that direction into components and layouts, speeding up implementation and later iterations. I review and refine the final result myself.

research.title: Finding my way through technologies and approaches
research.description: I use AI to compare libraries, architectures, and documentation. It narrows the options, then I validate the choice in the project's actual context.

integration.title: Starting integrations that require new research
integration.description: When connecting APIs, services, or less familiar systems, AI helps me explore the problem and prepare an initial solution to verify and adapt.

iteration.title: Leaving more room to evaluate the result
iteration.description: Refactoring and repetitive changes take less time when I can compare alternatives quickly. I use the saved time to check behavior and refine the solution.

infrastructure.title: My projects, available online
infrastructure.modeLabel: Explore the areas hosted on my personal VPS
infrastructure.detailLabel: WHY I USE A PERSONAL VPS

apps.title: Online applications, not just local demos
apps.description: I use an IONOS VPS to host my web apps, APIs, and some personal services. It lets me keep several projects online at a reasonable cost and, more importantly, gives me hands-on experience with what comes after local development: deployment, Linux, service configuration, updates, and monitoring.

api.title: Backend services under my control
api.description: Hosting APIs in the same environment gives me hands-on experience with backend processes, service configuration, and communication between frontend and server.

facts.label: PURPOSE
facts.value: APIs and services for personal applications

data.title: Data and continuity are part of the system
data.description: Running persistent data and services makes responsibilities like configuration, backups, security, and service continuity tangible.

experiments.title: A lab for trying real ideas
experiments.description: The VPS is also a place to try automations and small services without turning my local computer into the production environment.

boundary.title: I keep my personal projects separate from client projects

environments.label: PERSONAL // VPS
environments.title: My VPS
environments.description: I use a personal VPS to keep my projects, APIs, and services online. I develop them in my free time. It is also my test environment: I can experiment with Linux, deployments, configuration, monitoring, and service management beyond local development. I like following a project beyond the code, seeing how it performs once published, and learning to manage the infrastructure behind it.

environments.label: CLIENT // DEDICATED ENVIRONMENT
environments.title: Infrastructure suited to the project
environments.description: I do not reuse my personal infrastructure for client projects. The environment is chosen and configured around the project’s needs, required services, and where it will be used. It could be a dedicated VPS, a cloud service, or infrastructure already available at the client’s organization. The goal is to keep each project independent, easy to manage, and suited to the environment where it will run.
